The OSM[^osm] blog has an [interesting short article][article] on how OSM handles 
names in their data:

> Whether you are from, Saint-Louis-du-Ha! Ha!, Springfield or Ea names are 
important. They help us identify where we are, where we are from and where we 
want to go to. Almost everything has a name and OpenStreetMap volunteers have 
mapped 115 million names.

The article covers how OSM handles local names, official names, and names in 
multiple languages. It also covers how the map on <https://www.openstreetmap.org> 
displays names: 

> On the default layer of the www.openstreetmap.org website (osm-carto) we don’t 
show different names based on where you are, this means everyone will see the 
name of the feature in the local language. 

This is obviously different from many commercial web map providers.


[article]: https://blog.openstreetmap.org/2026/09/13/whats-in-a-name-naming-things-in-openstreetmap/

[^osm]: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), a collaborative, 
open-licensed map of the world.
